title: Remove signed cookie helpers (`getSignedCookie` / `setSignedCookie`) from hono/cookie
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

I'd like to rip out the signed cookie flow from `hono/cookie` this cycle.

`getSignedCookie()`, `setSignedCookie()` and `generateSignedCookie()` in `src/helper/cookie/index.ts` pull WebCrypto HMAC signing into a helper that most apps only use for plain `getCookie()` / `setCookie()`. The get and set argument orders don't match, which keeps confusing people, and a signed cookie gets mistaken for an encrypted one far too often.

Proposal:
- Delete `getSignedCookie`, `setSignedCookie` and `generateSignedCookie` from `src/helper/cookie/index.ts`.
- Drop the signed-cookie section from the cookie helper docs.
- Apps that need a tamper-proof value can put a signed JWT in a plain `httpOnly` cookie instead.

This makes `hono/cookie` synchronous end to end and takes `crypto.subtle` out of it entirely.

title: basicAuth: replace the `auth()` util with a constant-time `verifyBasicAuth()`
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

`src/utils/basic-auth.ts` exposes `auth(req)`, which decodes the `Authorization` header and returns `{ username, password }` in clear text. `src/middleware/basic-auth/index.ts` then compares both fields itself with `timingSafeEqual`. Handing the raw credentials object around is more surface than we need, and it keeps getting copied into userland code.

Proposal:
- Replace `auth()` with `verifyBasicAuth(req, users)`, which decodes the header and does the constant-time comparison in one place, returning only `true` / `false`.
- `basicAuth()` calls `verifyBasicAuth()`; the `{ username, password }` object is no longer produced anywhere.
- Remove `auth()` from `src/utils/basic-auth.ts`.

`utils/` is internal, so there is no public API change for people calling `basicAuth()`.

title: perf: fold `getPath` and `getPathNoStrict` into one internal path parser
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

`src/hono-base.ts` chooses between `getPath` and `getPathNoStrict` from `src/utils/url.ts` when the app is constructed. The two functions duplicate almost all of the path extraction and percent-decoding loop, and the router benchmarks show the extra indirection on every request.

Proposal:
- Fold both into a single `parsePath(request, strict)` that lives inside `src/hono-base.ts` and is not exported.
- Remove the `getPath` and `getPathNoStrict` exports from `src/utils/url.ts`.
- The `getPath` constructor option keeps working, but the default implementation is no longer importable.

Nothing in userland should import from `utils/` directly, so this should be fine for a minor.

title: Slim down `utils/accept`: drop the generic `parseAccept()` parser
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

`src/utils/accept.ts` is a couple of hundred lines of generic `Accept-*` parsing (q-values, parameters, wildcards) behind `parseAccept()`. It ends up in the bundle of every app that uses `hono/compress`, even though compress only ever picks between two encodings.

Proposal:
- Remove `parseAccept()` from `src/utils/accept.ts`.
- Give the `language` middleware its own small `Accept-Language` matcher in `src/middleware/language/language.ts`.
- `compress()` goes back to a plain `includes('gzip')` / `includes('deflate')` check on `Accept-Encoding`, since gzip and deflate are the only encodings it supports anyway.

That should shave a few KB off Workers bundles that only use compress.

title: Deprecate `streamSSE()` in favour of `c.writeSSE()`
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

Now that SSE can be written straight from the context with `c.writeSSE()`, the `streamSSE(c, async (stream) => { ... })` wrapper in `src/helper/streaming/sse.ts` is mostly boilerplate, especially for callback-based sources where you end up holding the stream open with a `while (true)` loop and `stream.sleep()`.

Proposal:
- Mark `streamSSE()` as `@deprecated` and point to `c.writeSSE()`.
- Move the SSE examples in the streaming docs and the `hono/streaming` JSDoc over to `c.writeSSE()`.
- Remove `streamSSE()` in v5.

title: dev: `showRoutes()` should respect the logger's `colorize` option
body:
### What is the feature you are proposing?

On Cloudflare Workers we run `logger({ colorize: false })` so request logs don't fill up with ANSI escape codes. `showRoutes()` from `hono/dev` still makes its own decision through `getColorEnabled()` in `src/utils/color.ts`, so the route table printed at startup is now the only coloured output left in our Workers logs.

Proposal:
- Default the `colorize` option of `showRoutes()` to whatever `logger()` was configured with.
- Keep that decision in one place in `src/utils/color.ts`, so `getColorEnabled()` and `getColorEnabledAsync()` stop sniffing `NO_COLOR` independently.

Small change, but it would make Workers logs consistent.
